briefing:
# Infosys Pre-Meeting Briefing: 17 November 2026

## Executive Summary

Infosys enters the 17 November 2026 meeting after a 30-day window (16 October to 15 November 2026) dominated by its Q2 FY27 results and a narrowed full-year revenue guidance. Revenue growth guidance was cut to 1% to 2% constant currency from 1.5% to 3% ([Thomas, 2026](https://www.briefs.co/news/infosys-cuts-2027-revenue-outlook-as-clients-tighten-tech-bu)). Underlying operating indicators were mixed: AI revenue accelerated, large-deal bookings were strong, but volume and pricing remained under pressure ([Investing.com, n.d.](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-infosys-q2-2026-beats-revenue-cuts-outlook-93CH-4969756); [BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23)). Shareholder-related events, including an interim dividend and a record date, were routine.

**My assessment:** The guidance cut should be read less as a demand collapse and more as a deliberate trade-off. Management is prioritising contract economics over volume, and it is explicitly absorbing AI-driven productivity deflation. The central question for the meeting is whether AI is becoming additive to revenue growth or mainly a source of price compression. The evidence so far supports both interpretations, and the company's own commentary does not resolve the question.

## Scope, Sources, and Verification Approach

The briefing covers the window of 16 October to 15 November 2026. Sources were ranked by reliability. Company-issued materials (the PR Newswire release and the earnings-call transcript) and established financial media (Investing.com, Briefs, and Livemint) were weighted above secondary commentary (LinkedIn posts, aggregators, and video titles). Where secondary sources conflict, this is flagged. Items outside the window or without a verifiable date are listed separately in the final section.

## Key Changes in the Last 30 Days

### Financial Performance and Guidance

The headline change was the revised FY2027 guidance. For the year ending March 2027, Infosys now guides to 1% to 2% constant-currency growth, down from 1.5% to 3% in July. The new range lags the 2.03% analyst consensus and pushed Infosys ADRs down as much as 7.6% in early New York trading on 23 October ([Thomas, 2026](https://www.briefs.co/news/infosys-cuts-2027-revenue-outlook-as-clients-tighten-tech-bu)).

The Q2 FY27 headline metrics are summarised below.

| Metric | Reported Figure | Source | Reliability Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q2 constant-currency revenue growth | 1.5% YoY; 1.2% QoQ | [BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23) | Aggregator; consistent with analyst commentary |
| Operating margin | 21% | [BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23); [InsiderFinance, 2026](https://www.insiderfinance.io/news/infosys-q2-results-ai-up-guidance-cut) | Two sources agree |
| Operating margin guidance | 20% to 22% (unchanged) | [Bose, n.d.](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/devam-bose-193235163_for-infosys-q2fy27-activity-7520050126766157824-Pbfl) | Individual commentary |
| Free cash flow | $922M (BigGo) or $928M (LinkedIn), down 15.7% YoY | [BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23); [Bose, n.d.](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/devam-bose-193235163_for-infosys-q2fy27-activity-7520050126766157824-Pbfl) | Sources conflict; verify against the filing |
| Net profit | ₹7,823 crore, up about 6% YoY | [Bose, n.d.](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/devam-bose-193235163_for-infosys-q2fy27-activity-7520050126766157824-Pbfl) | Individual commentary |
| Revenue | ₹49,244 crore, up about 11% YoY (rupee terms); $5.145B | [Bose, n.d.](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/devam-bose-193235163_for-infosys-q2fy27-activity-7520050126766157824-Pbfl) | Rupee growth is not comparable to constant-currency growth |
| Cash yield | Approximately 6.9% | [Investing.com, n.d.](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-infosys-q2-2026-beats-revenue-cuts-outlook-93CH-4969756) | Company call |
| DSO | 64 days, down 7 days YoY | [Investing.com, n.d.](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-infosys-q2-2026-beats-revenue-cuts-outlook-93CH-4969756) | Company call |
| Effective tax rate (FY) | 29% to 30% | [Investing.com, n.d.](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-infosys-q2-2026-beats-revenue-cuts-outlook-93CH-4969756) | Company call |

Management attributed the guidance reduction to several factors. The CFO stated that "our Q2 has been softer, and our volume continues to remain softer," and cited pricing pressure from competitive intensity and higher client demands for productivity ([BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23)). The CFO also said that offshoring changes and a decision not to pursue a large European manufacturing deal that did not meet return expectations together reduced growth guidance by about 2% ([BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23)). The company also flagged lower working days in H2 as an impact ([Investing.com, n.d.](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-infosys-q2-2026-beats-revenue-cuts-outlook-93CH-4969756)).

Analysts pressed on the guidance, with one noting that the full-year outlook was the weakest in seven years and the slowest growth pace in at least three years ([BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23)).

### Deals and AI Monetisation

Large-deal bookings in Q2 totalled $5.2 billion, including a net-new mega deal worth more than $2.0 billion over seven years and a $1 billion renewal ([InsiderFinance, 2026](https://www.insiderfinance.io/news/infosys-q2-results-ai-up-guidance-cut); [BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23)). One secondary source reports that 62% of the pipeline was net-new business ([Bose, n.d.](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/devam-bose-193235163_for-infosys-q2fy27-activity-7520050126766157824-Pbfl)). Analysts noted that the mega-deal ramp-up will not begin until the latter part of the fiscal year ([BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23)).

AI revenue rose 29% sequentially and represented 10.5% of total revenue, up from 8.2% in the prior quarter ([BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23); [InsiderFinance, 2026](https://www.insiderfinance.io/news/infosys-q2-results-ai-up-guidance-cut)). CEO Salil Parekh stated that AI is "giving us the growth" while also "seeing the compression" from competitive intensity, and that almost all deals of $50 million or more now include AI ([Thomas, 2026](https://www.briefs.co/news/infosys-cuts-2027-revenue-outlook-as-clients-tighten-tech-bu)). On the call, he described AI-related services as a secular opportunity, in contrast to the finite nature of a particular large deal ([Investing.com, n.d.](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-infosys-q2-2026-beats-revenue-cuts-outlook-93CH-4969756)). He cited a $300 billion addressable market for AI services ([BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23)).

### Shareholder Returns and Workforce

Infosys declared an interim dividend of ₹26 per share for FY27, up from ₹23 in the prior year. The record date was 3 November 2026, and payment was scheduled for 11 November 2026 ([Sethi, 2026](https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/infosys-dividend-2026-record-date-tomorrow-know-dividend-payout-yield-history-returns-11793585489373.html)). Payment status on 11 November is not confirmed in the materials reviewed.

Shares had declined 27.29% year-to-date and 20.06% over the past year as of early November ([Sethi, 2026](https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/infosys-dividend-2026-record-date-tomorrow-know-dividend-payout-yield-history-returns-11793585489373.html)).

On headcount, net headcount rose by about 4,400 in H1. The company hired about 13,000 freshers in H1 against an FY2027 target of about 20,000. Attrition fell to 12.7% from 13.0% sequentially. Utilisation was 85.4% including trainees, but 81.9% excluding trainees, reflecting fresher intake ([Investing.com, n.d.](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-infosys-q2-2026-beats-revenue-cuts-outlook-93CH-4969756)). Compensation increases took effect 26 October, with a second phase scheduled for 27 January 2027 ([Investing.com, n.d.](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-infosys-q2-2026-beats-revenue-cuts-outlook-93CH-4969756)).

### Partnerships and Launches

Infosys announced a strategic collaboration with Columbia University focused on deep research and business value. The release itself was retrieved without a verifiable publication date, so its timing relative to the window cannot be confirmed ([Infosys, n.d.](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/infosys-and-columbia-university-launch-strategic-collaboration-across-deep-research-to-drive-innovation-and-unlock-business-value-302895969.html)).

### Market and Macro Context

Several market headlines in the same period bear on Infosys's outlook, though they are not company-specific:

- **Demand sentiment in India:** A 14 November headline reported that India's market was recovering as AI enthusiasm cooled and foreign capital returned ([Briefs, 2026](https://www.briefs.co/news/infosys-cuts-2027-revenue-outlook-as-clients-tighten-tech-bu)).
- **AI infrastructure in India:** AirTrunk filed plans for two large data campus projects in Andhra Pradesh, which may support demand for data-centre-related services ([Briefs, 2026](https://www.briefs.co/news/infosys-cuts-2027-revenue-outlook-as-clients-tighten-tech-bu)).
- **Currency and rates:** The dollar rallied to a one-month high as traders increased Fed hike wagers ([Briefs, 2026](https://www.briefs.co/news/infosys-cuts-2027-revenue-outlook-as-clients-tighten-tech-bu)). For an exporter that reports in rupees and dollars, this matters for reported versus constant-currency growth.
- **AI as a systemic risk:** A Fed survey placed AI at the top of financial-system risks ([Briefs, 2026](https://www.briefs.co/news/infosys-cuts-2027-revenue-outlook-as-clients-tighten-tech-bu)).

## Analyst Assessment

Based on the evidence above, my view is as follows.

**1. The guidance cut reflects deliberate selectivity, but it is also a volume problem.** Management's explanation combines discipline (declining a large European manufacturing deal) with structural factors (offshoring and softer volume). The 2% impact attributed to the offshoring change and the European deal is material relative to a 1% to 2% range. Without the deal decision, the revised range would be considerably less conservative. The company has not provided a breakdown of how much of the 2% is recoverable.

**2. AI is currently growing revenue, but its deflationary effect is not yet netted out.** The 29% sequential rise in AI revenue is significant. However, management cited AI-driven productivity deflation as a reason for lower guidance. The company's own language, "giving us the growth" alongside "seeing the compression," indicates that the net effect is still being measured. Until pricing data is disclosed, I would treat AI as a gross growth driver with an uncertain net contribution.

**3. Bookings are strong, but conversion timing is the binding constraint.** The $5.2 billion in large deals is a positive signal of client willingness to commit. However, the mega-deal ramp is not expected to contribute meaningfully until the later part of the year. Revenue growth in H2 will depend on execution and on whether the company can offset weak volume.

**4. The margin and cash profile is a relative strength.** A stable 21% operating margin and a 6.9% cash yield suggest financial flexibility. The decline in free cash flow (reported at 15.7% YoY by one source) should be verified, since the reported figures differ between sources.

**5. Investor sentiment is pricing in a structural concern.** A 27% year-to-date decline in the share price is consistent with a market that views the growth gap as persistent rather than cyclical. Management needs to demonstrate that AI-led revenue can compound faster than pricing pressure.

## Risks and Watch Items

| Risk | Indicator to Monitor | Source Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Continued volume softness | Constant-currency growth in Q3 FY27 relative to the 1% to 2% range | [BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23) |
| AI-driven pricing deflation | Revenue per employee and pricing commentary on AI deals | [Thomas, 2026](https://www.briefs.co/news/infosys-cuts-2027-revenue-outlook-as-clients-tighten-tech-bu) |
| Mega-deal ramp delay | Timing of revenue recognition from the $2B+ contract | [BigGo Finance, 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_INFY_2026-10-23) |
| Currency volatility | Gap between reported and constant-currency growth | [Briefs, 2026](https://www.briefs.co/news/infosys-cuts-2027-revenue-outlook-as-clients-tighten-tech-bu) |
| Fresher hiring shortfall | Progress against the 20,000-fresher FY27 target (13,000 hired in H1) | [Investing.com, n.d.](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-infosys-q2-2026-beats-revenue-cuts-outlook-93CH-4969756) |
| Wage cost pressure | Effect of the January 2027 compensation phase on margins | [Investing.com, n.d.](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-infosys-q2-2026-beats-revenue-cuts-outlook-93CH-4969756) |
